levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named and its effect on the conclusion is stated.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named, tested against the scenario, and bounded.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The conclusion is stated as certain when the scenario does not support that.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known and how it limits the conclusion.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known, how it limits the conclusion, and what would resolve it.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: Recommend for or against this purchase for Solveig. State the monthly figure you are relying on, name the assumptions the analysis rests on, and identify the one figure whose failure would most damage the conclusion.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: States a recommendation and relies on the $562.59 true monthly cost rather than the $342.60 payment, or explains why a different figure is the right one for the decision.
Names at least two load-bearing assumptions, such as the 15% depreciation holding, the running costs staying flat for five years, or the five-year holding period being kept to.
Identifies the most damaging failure and says why — most defensibly the $9,650.59 resale value, since it is the only figure recovered at the end and it rests entirely on the depreciation assumption.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the $33,755.41 five-year total and the 17.7% share of take-home pay.
Refers to the $219.99 gap between the true monthly cost and the advertised payment.
lookFors: The recommendation is decided and the figure behind it is named.
The assumptions listed appear in the analysis rather than being general cautions.
Either recommendation is acceptable; what is scored is whether financing, running costs, and resale are all carried through the reasoning.
judgment.commonMisconception: Judging affordability against the payment a lender quotes rather than against the cost of the commitment.

judgment.prompt: The resale value is the only figure in this analysis that reduces the cost. Explain what makes it different in kind from the others, and say what the true monthly cost would be if the vehicle turned out to be worth nothing at the end.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that every other figure is a known price or a quoted term, while the resale value is a forecast that will not be tested until year five.
Computes the alternative correctly, giving a true monthly cost of about $723.43 if the resale value were zero, and notes that this is more than double the advertised payment.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $9,650.59 resale figure and the $33,755.41 total when explaining the effect of its failure.
lookFors: The response distinguishes a quoted figure from a projected one.
The recomputation is attempted with figures rather than described qualitatively.
judgment.commonMisconception: Treating an expected resale value as a certainty because it appears in the same table as the contracted payments.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
oracle.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic over BigInt; no binary floating point
oracle.limits: Recomputation establishes that the key follows from the stated figures. It does not by itself establish that the model chosen is the right model for the scenario; that is carried by the per-item reasoning, the parameter-visibility check, and human review.
